claims.text: The initial HEA multilayers have semi-coherent or incoherent interfaces.
Introducing a thin Nb interlayer will enhance interface coherency in HEA multilayers.
Nb-enhanced interface coherency will mediate the transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep.
The effect on creep behavior will scale with Nb interlayer thickness.
Both diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep can be activated under the proposed high-temperature, constant-stress conditions.
Nb has lattice parameters intermediate enough relative to the HEA layers to promote coherent interfaces.
Nb diffusivity promotes the formation of coherent interfaces.
Improved interface coherency alters interfacial atomic-diffusion barriers.
At high temperatures, the Nb-containing multilayer will exhibit diffusion-dominated creep.
At lower temperatures, coherent interfaces will facilitate dislocation slip.
Facilitated dislocation slip will enable a controlled transition between the two creep regimes.
An optimized Nb interlayer will produce a measurable shift in creep behavior relative to a multilayer without Nb.
An optimized Nb interlayer will reduce the creep rate in the dislocation-mediated regime relative to the baseline multilayer.
HEA multilayers without Nb have a less pronounced or less controlled transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep.
The proposed effect requires HEA layers that are compatible with Nb in lattice matching.
Unexpected phase formation or interface incompatibility would limit the proposed effect.
